entries.name: Harness kit: one set-up, in Rust, that holds a second person's sessions to the method
entries.what: One wrapper command builds eleven Rust programs and wires six of them as hooks into a project's own settings (the clone or a repository of hers): the start hook that loads the short rules, the window ceiling, the model and effort by kind of job, the count of helpers at once, token limits with a basis and a cap, and the limit on review rounds. The set-up also writes the three settings this project runs with. With it: the queue for heavy commands, test files side by side, units in their own copies landing through the check in one order, a counter of what each helper cost, the short rules, the README, and the coverage table with one row for every item of the method. Needs the Rust toolchain and git.
entries.number: Each hook program passes its hook's test file (135, 49, 42, 30, 30, 10 and 8 cases); the set-up 22 tests holding 65 cases; the parallel commands 6; the clean-clone check passes every line on Windows; the coverage table holds 280 rows, none without a mark
entries.gain: one hook call 2.8 to 6.8 times faster than through its JavaScript hook (median of 20, one PC); no gain on tokens or quality measured

entries.name: The hooks' test files drive either form; the routing fix; efforts in the routes file
entries.what: The hooks' test files run against the JavaScript hook or, with KIT_HOOK_BIN_DIR, against its Rust program; a test file of its own for the tier hook. The tier hook looks a kind up only among the routes file's own kinds. The routes file lists the efforts each route allows.
entries.number: Test files against the programs: window-ceiling 135, fanout-gate 49, creep-gate 42, count-gate 30, tier hook 30 with 1 skipped; against the JavaScript the cases that need no kit mode pass
